rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this round pushes obfuscation intensity up on a program with only one real function (main, 266 bytes) where size and runtime budgets are generous: FLA gets the highest SecurityGain since control-flow flattening dominates reverse-engineering resistance on small straight-line-ish code, backed by BCF and SUB for opaque predicate and arithmetic-layer diversity; SPLIT and IBR add cheap structural diversity with low risk, so they run broadly; ICALL and IGV stay moderate because this program has few call sites and globals, limiting their upside and giving them the highest correctness risk of indirect conversion. RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are kept low across the board so cost sensitivity does not suppress application, while CorrectnessRisk weights remain nonzero so passes are skipped on constructs where they could break semantics, preserving the correct execution observed in round 0.
